about: The build ladder on sheet A14. A recording capability (R) and an early, offline need test on one person (N1, N2) are proposed to come first {{dec:need-test-order}}; then two tracks, perception (rungs 1–6) and light (rungs 7–8), meet at the coordinator (rung 9). Each rung builds one primitive into today's loop as built, behind the record that primitive writes; the gate (or, where the sheets set no threshold, the rule that sets it), each metric's orientation, unit and margin, and the record version are written before the rung starts. Thresholds are A13's per-link targets (Target · validate) unless a rung says the sheets set none. Where a rung needs a part that comes later, it uses a fixed, logged stand-in. Once N2 has run, after each replaced input (detector boxes, tracker association, bundles with causal routing, geometric fields) its frozen held-out gate is re-run with the scoring rules fixed; a session used for diagnosis moves to development, and once a diagnosis informs tuning, confirmation needs a fresh, independent held-out set. Where a gate depends on an owner choice still open, the rung links to the register and that part is not admitted until the owner decides. Inline markup: **bold**, `code`, [[R5]] repo-note chips, {{dec:…}} pending-decision tags.

rungs.name: Recording capability
rungs.outText: retained single-person den sessions with validated capture metadata (no record defined yet)
rungs.replaces: Recordings without qualified capture metadata: the den capture server answers with its latest RGBD frame only and relays only the RTSP video onward [[R2]]; the Lab recording controller on the Victoria Jetson has made den Lab recordings [[R9]], but its encoded timeline is not validated capture time. Split out of rung 0's recording scope.
rungs.tested: A capability, which needs the owner's approval, to keep single-person den sessions on a validated capture clock, not depending on depth. Who may appear (guests included), deletion, blurring in retained data, and whether gold sessions keep their metering frames are open {{dec:recording-retention}}. It can start first, alongside rung 0.
rungs.gate: Every retained session carries validated capture metadata, checked by a method and tolerance written before the run; none is set yet. Intervals with a second person in view are cut and reported. This step is not admitted until the owner decides {{dec:recording-retention}}.
rungs.loop: Not applicable: recording changes nothing in the loop.
rungs.unblocks: N1's reference fixture and blind labels on retained sessions. It does not wait for rung 0's complete decision replay, which later coordinator and control claims still need.

rungs.name: Record and replay
rungs.replaces: Scattered memory of what happened: the brain keeps its newest 20 decisions with a 'why' [[R13]], LA writes JSONL ledgers [[R16]], and den_lighting records manual holds [[R14]].
rungs.tested: What today's loop writes, kept long-term: Frigate occupancy, Qwen's scene facts, the room's activity label, the brain's decisions with their 'why', den_lighting's commands with readback, mode and version as incumbent Decisions (`policy`, `actuator_domain = hue-den-4`, `actuation = shown`), each human action that opened or replaced a hold as one Correction (its `changes[]` and the hold it opened), hold-creation events and lifetimes, each session's exposure (`occupied_h`, `occupancy_source`, and den_lighting's mode as `mode_stratum`), and overrides made in the Home app. The rule table's virtual decisions go in a separate log. For gold-labelled sessions the metering frames are kept too {{dec:recording-retention}}. Keeping the camera recordings is step R.
rungs.gate: Every logged decision replays from its logged inputs and versions to the same `requested_scene`, and with its `hold_set` and step log (`applied_scene` per channel: status, readback, `steps[]`) to the same `applied_scene`, including dropped, stopped and repaired steps; den_lighting's incumbent Decisions replay too. From here on, a candidate whose decisions cannot be replayed is not promoted (A13), and each later rung adds its own record to the log before its gate is scored.
rungs.loop: Not applicable: this rung is the record the later replays run on.
rungs.unblocks: The coordinator's replay against the incumbent (rung 9). It also starts E1's numerator (den_lighting's holds, one Correction per human action) and the per-session exposure and per-action correction counts from which rung 11's exposure-adjusted planning value of φ is fitted; E1 as written runs at rungs 11 and 12. N1 and N2 do not wait for it.

rungs.name: A single-person reference, as two artifacts
rungs.outText: an input fixture and, kept apart from it, blind labels (no record defined yet; once scored, EvalRecord's gold_set.n1 holds them as two separately versioned, hashed artifacts)
rungs.replaces: Nothing. Den gold today is under a minute [[R18]]. This proposes moving the single-person part of rung 4 ahead of rungs 1–3; when N1 and N2 run is open {{dec:need-test-order}}.
rungs.tested: R's retained single-person sessions, with hard cases staged on purpose: a phone at the counter, wiping, sorting mail, a still reader, an idle seated person, low light. **The input fixture:** per-frame person boxes, drawn by the owner or from a fixed detector the owner audits, padded so the hands and the worked object stay in the crop; one constant id; and a static surface map (surface ids, types, declared heights, handheld and lap regions). Nothing time-varying enters it: no hand, contact or working-region marks, which would encode the onset into the input. **The labels**, made in a separate blind pass: engagement intervals, demand bands, and the shortcut and quiet cases, each with its labeller recorded.
rungs.gate: A written annotation protocol is fixed before labelling: the onset and offset definitions and the system state that onset delay is timed to {{dec:onset-protocol}}; the demand bands and their cut points {{dec:demand-gates}}; how uncertain labels are handled; who labels, blind, with an actor record {{dec:labelling}}; and a whole-session split into development and held-out parts before any tuning. The fixture and the labels are versioned and hashed separately before any estimator output is opened. This step is not admitted until the owner decides on recording, labelling and the onset protocol.
rungs.loop: Not applicable: a reference changes nothing in the loop.
rungs.unblocks: N2's scores. The fixture is a fixed input, not gold, and production need must pass again without it (rung 6).

rungs.name: Semantic need on one person, offline
rungs.replaces: Nothing in the loop. It is the earliest test of the riskiest premise: that den pixels show what light one person needs. Today one activity label covers the whole room [[R4]].
rungs.tested: N1's held-out sessions. N2 estimates only K7's semantic fields, `focused_engagement` and `visual_demand` with their confidences, for one anonymous person. Everything upstream is a frozen, versioned stand-in: N1's boxes and constant id, the static surface map, a fixed 2D pose and object detector, a frozen per-person interpreter request (the box in the latest frame), a frozen E3 field assignment, and A7's rule parameters at their starting values or tuned on development data. Hands-on-region and head-on-region become image-plane approximations, so N2 scores a declared variant of K7, not production K7. Requests go out offline at the declared single-track pace (one request per 4 s) and their service time is measured, not declared; only the capture-to-request schedule is emulated, from R's capture clock. The whole-room stills receipt (1.25 s median, 1.97 s p95) times a different workload, so it does not qualify the per-person requests [[R3]]. The detectors and Qwen run offline on LA only with the owner's permission, within the GPU admission rules [[R19]].
rungs.gate: A three-valued verdict, **feasible / not feasible / insufficient** (`feasible | not_feasible | insufficient`), written to an EvalRecord; nothing is promoted or changed in the loop. Fixed before the held-out set is opened: metric definitions with orientation and unit (A13 Gate 1), the onset definition, band cut points, per-band and per-case sample gates, floors for band competence and fine-demand misses {{dec:demand-gates}}, a shortcut-case criterion, the stand-in versions, the replay pacing and the interval level {{dec:promotion-margins}}. A13's targets (onset **≤ 3 s median**, early-off **≈ 0**, **ECE ≤ 0.1**) are starting values. An unmet sample gate means insufficient: record more sessions, never relax a threshold. No working-region, room-position, two-person or routed-timing claim. The onset gate is not admitted until the owner decides {{dec:onset-protocol}}: an onset marked at first hand contact and timed to 'engaged' behind K7's 5 s entry dwell misses a 3 s median target by construction, which is a protocol issue, not an inference failure.
rungs.loop: Not applicable: N2 changes nothing in the loop. Today's room label may be reported on the same sessions, with A13's qualifications (its replay needs the owner's go-ahead [[R4]]), but it is not the gate.
rungs.unblocks: If feasible: the perception rungs from rung 1, in an order the owner sets {{dec:need-test-order}}, with N2's frozen gate re-run after each replaced input. If not feasible: keep den_lighting, and do not start, or carry further, the production tracker, bundles or per-person optimizer on the strength of the need premise (which of the two applies depends on when N2 runs); diagnose by field and case first (a viewpoint-limited failure points to camera placement or registration; a still-reader failure to A7's weights and `θ_on`, revisited on development data; a demand-only failure to the interpreter input or another demand signal, then a fresh held-out set). The light track keeps its value either way. N2 also gives a provisional E3 split, biased toward geometry because the geometry is supplied.

rungs.name: Camera registration
rungs.replaces: An approximate one-person placement; the OAK-to-scan registration was refused [[R10]].
rungs.tested: Control points measured in the den, seen by the camera and found in the scan. Runs live in the den. It is proposed to follow N2 {{dec:need-test-order}}.
rungs.gate: The repo's rule for a verified registration, which A12 cites: three non-collinear control pairs plus two independent checks, **all within 5 cm**. The result is written to the RoomModel's camera entry with its method and version; that entry is what every later Observation's `transform_id` (`<camera_id>@<version>`) resolves to.
rungs.loop: Not yet: nothing reads the registration until rung 2.
rungs.unblocks: Room-frame observations, and a working-region error that measures the estimator rather than the registration.

rungs.name: Observations in the room frame
rungs.replaces: Detectors that live in the den loop held at operator_stop, where 115 of 228 results expired in one window [[R5]].
rungs.tested: Recorded evenings, with the detectors restarted on the owner's go-ahead.
rungs.gate: Every Observation carries its capture time, room position with covariance, validity and freshness; keypoint Observations also carry `joints_room` (per joint: position, covariance, support status and lift), `depth_ts` and a `transform_id` that resolves to a RoomModel camera entry. A depth frame too old for its capture is not used: the declared plane fallback applies, with a larger covariance, and the gap is flagged. Detector freshness: no threshold is set in the sheets; set one before the run, with R5's expiry rate as the baseline.
rungs.loop: Checkpoint, if N2 has already run {{dec:need-test-order}}: N2's frozen held-out gate is re-run with the detector's boxes in place of N1's, scoring rules unchanged. Otherwise nothing reads room-frame Observations until rung 3.

rungs.name: Tracks, from geometry
rungs.replaces: Per-frame `slot-N` ids with nothing linking a person across frames [[R7]].
rungs.tested: E2's geometry-only arm: 20–30 staged crossings and occlusions in the den, owner-annotated.
rungs.gate: **0 silent swaps**, meaning no identity switch while the tracker reported confidence; **IDF1 ≥ 0.9**. The sample's uncertainty is reported: 0 swaps in 20–30 crossings still allows a failure rate of about 14% (20 crossings) to 10% (30) at a one-sided 95% bound. E2's body-appearance and face arms need the owner's decision on rebuild principle 15 first (A5) {{dec:learning-permissions}}, so they are not part of this gate.
rungs.loop: Checkpoint, if N2 has already run {{dec:need-test-order}}: N2's frozen gate is re-run with tracker association in place of the constant id. Otherwise not yet: rung 4's two-person marks are made per track, and the loop first reads tracks at rung 5.
rungs.unblocks: Per-person gold marks, and everything per person. If geometry alone misses the gate, session appearance becomes its own rung, after the owner's decision {{dec:learning-permissions}}.

rungs.name: A two-person gold set, per track
rungs.outText: gold annotations (no record defined yet; EvalRecord's gold_set and sample_gate fields record them once scored)
rungs.replaces: Nothing. Den gold today is under a minute [[R18]]; N1 holds the single-person part.
rungs.tested: Independent two-person den sessions, labelled blind and split by whole session: same-surface work, a crossing behind the armchair, a guest (with the owner's recording permission {{dec:recording-retention}}) and low light. The owner marks, per track: when someone starts and stops working; the worked patch, as an outline with its placement uncertainty, on every need interval that service will score, one person or two, drawn from the hands and the worked object, never from where the light falls, and kept as a label only (each mark is an `R_eval` with `source: gold_mark`, counted in `gold_set.regions`); the demand class (fine, casual, none); and posture, hands and head pose for the per-field checks. Staged sessions also get independently measured head and shoulder positions {{dec:envelope-parameters}}. Who labels, and whether every need interval or only a sample gets a mark, are open {{dec:labelling}}.
rungs.gate: Per demand band (fine, casual, none), a minimum number of independent episodes across distinct sessions and days, set before labelling closes; none is set yet {{dec:demand-gates}}. Start from the repo's gate for V-JEPA probes (at least 3 held-out sessions over at least 2 days, at least 480 labelled seconds) and A13's size order (a few hours of video, hundreds of intervals). Labels a model made may train but never score. The label set, the marks' geometry included, is versioned and hashed into EvalRecord's `gold_set` before any candidate output is opened; marks carry no hash of their own. Each mark's `placement_sd` (cm, in the surface plane) is tested against `τ_R`, and how closely a mark must be placed is open {{dec:reference-geometry}}.
rungs.loop: Not applicable: the gold set changes nothing in the loop.
rungs.unblocks: Honest two-person scores for rung 6's need and perception checks, for E3, and later for the student (E4); and the owner's marks, where service is measured at rungs 9–11.

rungs.name: Person bundles
rungs.replaces: Nothing in the loop yet: Qwen keeps getting today's whole-room stills until rung 6 reads bundles. A router v0 sets the per-person rate within today's caps (at most one request every 4 s and 15 a minute, one in flight; A6), round-robin across tracks, versioned as a router rule.
rungs.tested: Recorded evenings, and E2's crossings for the association flags.
rungs.gate: Each bundle covers its time window with its sources aligned; `association_safe` is false through every annotated crossing; missing sources are flagged rather than waited for. `keypoint_series` entries copy each association-gated Observation verbatim: `obs_id`, `ts`, `camera_id`, `transform_id`, keypoints and `joints_room`. No latency threshold is set for bundles yet.
rungs.loop: Checkpoint, if N2 has already run {{dec:need-test-order}}: N2's frozen gate is re-run with causal routing and real capture timestamps, one track and then two, including real availability under round-robin, admission refusals and the 30 s back-off. Otherwise not yet: bundles are read from rung 6.

rungs.name: Person need
rungs.replaces: One activity label for the whole room [[R4]], and the whole-room stills Qwen gets today. A fixed adapter feeds today's rule table from PersonState and keeps its rule that two or more people get ambient light, so this rung delivers per-person state, not yet per-person light. LightState is absent until rung 7 and logged as missing.
rungs.tested: The held-out gold sessions, one person (N1) and two (rung 4); three location-versus-behavior cases (a phone at the counter, wiping the counter, sorting mail); the A/B swap, where B's bundle comes from another session while A's stays fixed; and held-support fixtures: overlap, occlusion, a heartbeat without new support, deadband confirmation and reacquisition, with missing and stale geometry.
rungs.gate: Working region **median ≤ 15 cm, p90 ≤ 30 cm**. Engagement onset **≤ 3 s median**, timed as the onset protocol defines; that part is not admitted until the owner decides {{dec:onset-protocol}}. Early-off **≈ 0**. Visual demand: fine-demand recall per episode (abstaining or stale counts as a miss), false-fine rate and per-band coverage above floors set on the development split, per-band sample gates met {{dec:demand-gates}}, and **ECE ≤ 0.1**. Posture, hands and head pose: no threshold is set; set per field from a baseline (A13). Head position and its covariance cover the measured references, envelope containment is scored at `t_exec` by posture and support status, and the missing and stale fallbacks refuse as declared; their thresholds are pre-registered {{dec:envelope-parameters}}. Each field keeps its own support time, and a heartbeat never moves any field's support time. Before the coordinator joins: A's fields do not move beyond their own noise when B's bundle is swapped, the same-surface, crossing and shortcut cases pass, and N2's frozen gate is re-run on production need. A13 Gate 2's latency and GPU memory budgets hold, with sustained operation beside voice [[R19]].
rungs.loop: Non-inferior to today's room label recomputed on the same held-out sessions (the held activity stage replayed, with the owner's go-ahead [[R4]]), each metric's orientation and δ fixed before the run {{dec:promotion-margins}}; none is set yet. The baseline's version (wire, validity window, judge version, smoothing) is pinned and recorded, and its coverage and accuracy are computed together on the same accepted seconds against owner-confirmed labels only. Three facts from the 2026-10-10 accuracy note are context, not the baseline (A13): its only scored session answered on 16–19% of seconds under about 1 s validity, with about 0.51 accuracy, mostly against Qwen-proposed labels; replayed with facts-bound validity, coverage is 0.43–0.49, accuracy not recomputed; and only the computer interval was owner-confirmed.
rungs.unblocks: Targets per person. Before the rung, E3 runs offline on the development sessions and may move fields to rules on geometry (PersonState.sources); every other field stays with Qwen, now per person, as in build order step 1, and E3 is re-checked here. Replacing Qwen wholesale is the student's rung.

rungs.name: Measure light
rungs.replaces: Nothing measures light today. Camera footprint calibration failed three runs [[R12]], and no lux sensor feeds any lighting logic [[R17]]. Reflectance is assumed (A12).
rungs.tested: Live in the empty den, following A14's rule that probes must not look like people: den_lighting paused, every probe logged as a non-human change and excluded from corrections; afterwards den_lighting's saved normal scene is written back from a pre-probe snapshot before `den_lighting.resume_automatic` clears the holds, because it learns unrecognised writes as its normal scene even while paused. A run aborts on the occupancy gate or on any state change it did not send, and no remaining flash or restore overwrites a light a person changed (A12). E7 on the four Hue bulbs with locked exposure and white balance, linear values and an all-off frame subtracted. E8 on at least two days: a grey card of known reflectance with the meter in the card's plane at each meter point (desk and sofa); the known-card round trip and an exposure-invariance check before scoring; on day 1 the camera scale `k_L` is fitted from one card and one meter reading at the card, and the other meter points and later days are held back as checks, with a day of window daylight. A grey-card reflectance pass at every working region the coordinator will target, counter-1 at least (A12), written to the RoomModel's surfaces.
rungs.gate: Precondition: the known-card round trip recovers the card (A12: `C_card` 100 nc, ρ_card 0.18 and `E_meter` 174.533 lx give `k_L` 0.100 (cd/m²)/nc and 174.533 lx back), written to `CalibrationRecord.checks.round_trip`, and the normalisation version matches (`normalisation_version` `meter-norm/v1`). Then held-out days and meter points not used to fit `k_L` stay within a meter tolerance stated in lux, fixed before day 1 {{dec:photometry-commissioning}}; the sheets set none. A common scale cancels from relative residuals and camera-fitted relative-error scores, so those can neither be corrupted by a scale error nor detect it; absolute lux values and errors, fixed physical thresholds and independently scaled physics or datasheet terms do scale. Rung 7 needs both the round trip and independent held-out card and meter checks in lux, as future qualification.
rungs.loop: Occupied-camera checkpoint, moved here from rung 10 and split in two: first a capture-side coexistence check, on single-person sessions recorded with metering frames interleaved and scored by N2's frozen estimator; then, once production perception runs, rungs 2–6 non-inferior on their own gates with metering interleaved, each metric's orientation and δ fixed before the run {{dec:promotion-margins}}. Light state itself is first read at rung 8.
rungs.unblocks: Absolute light targets for the coordinator, and verify. A passing relative score (rung 8) establishes neither of this rung's checks.

rungs.name: Light model
rungs.replaces: Aim math, a beam trace and hand-drawn footprints; the virtual den sums one bounce with assumed photometry [[R12]] [[R15]].
rungs.tested: Held-out mixed scenes on the Hue bulbs, scenes the per-channel basis was not fitted on, in the empty den under the same probe rule as rung 7; then occupied hold-outs for the visibility term.
rungs.gate: Relative error against camera estimates: **median 8%, p90 19%**. The basis is fitted from the same camera captures, so `k_L` and ρ cancel in this relative score: it does not wait on rung 7's absolute anchor, and it cannot detect a camera-scale error; rung 7's held-out meter check does. The occupied visibility is stated as `V_total = (V_direct·E_dir + E_ind)/B` for `B > 0`, an unchanged-indirect approximation, and qualified on occupied hold-outs. Relative and absolute qualification are reported separately.
rungs.loop: Not yet: the model is read from rung 9.
rungs.unblocks: A coordinator that predicts before it acts.

rungs.name: Coordinator v0
rungs.replaces: The rule table and over-shoulder aim planner, on virtual output [[R13]]. On the four Hue bulbs the scene policy it competes with is den_lighting's [[R14]]. Look and Preference are fixed stand-ins until their later rungs: one seed Look (A9's guidance table, guardrails and glare limit, versioned), and a level factor held at 1 with `mired_shift` and `contrast_shift` at 0, logged.
rungs.tested: Replayed evenings on the Hue fixture set (`actuator_domain = hue-den-4`, `actuation = replay`, with a `policy` such as `coordinator@k16-v0`) with rung 8's model, then a shadow run (`actuation = shadow`). Each evening's hold set and actuator state come from rung 0's log, and held channels are pinned at read-back in both arms; candidate and incumbent scenes pass through the same rung 8 model version. Deterministic hold fixtures (cases V6–V8 and V62–V64: a dim and a brighten held, a hold between solve and send, a shared bulb dimmed while another person still needs light, gaming entry and exit under a hold, overlapping holds) have expected results that depend on the compensation option, so they are not admitted as pass or fail until the owner decides {{dec:compensation}}. On a simulated spot only, with no physical path [[R11]]: the execution cases V9a–V9h, V9k and V9l, and a person entering a held beam's envelope, V65(b) {{dec:moving-spot}} {{dec:unset-hold-fields}} {{dec:local-completion}} {{dec:unknown-aim-on}} {{dec:mid-execution}} {{dec:manual-vs-safety}}. The virtual den's replay against the rule table uses assumed photometry and is E10's separate synthetic study; it does not count as this check.
rungs.gate: On replay against the scenes the frozen den_lighting version actually showed on the same evenings, both through rung 8's model: the candidate's anticipation and stability rates, recorded as replay surrogates. The incumbent scores 0 and 1 on them by construction, so each is a floor fixed before the run, not a difference. Predicted service coverage and missed service at the owner's marks on gold-labelled replay sessions, labelled 'predicted, replay surrogate', are reported, not gated. Every Decision carries its requested and applied scenes and the recipients of its applied scene, reproducible on replay; replay reproduces exclusions from `state_id`s with `field_support`, the envelope version and the logged `t_exec`. Hard constraints hold on free channels, with every conflict logged in `hard_conflicts`. Every decision replays, and each takes **under 100 ms**, aims included (A9). Real-light use is not part of this gate: it comes at rung 11, after verify.
rungs.loop: Non-inferior on every link it touches (A13 Gate 1), each metric's orientation and δ fixed before the run {{dec:promotion-margins}}; none is set yet. No live-rate claim and no corrections per hour: the comparator is den_lighting's shown Hue scenes (frozen as for rung 11), with held fixtures kept held in the candidate's scene. The rule table's virtual decisions are E10's separate synthetic study (`comparator.kind = synthetic`) and do not count.
rungs.unblocks: Verify, and per-person light once rung 11 hands it the bulbs.

rungs.name: Verify
rungs.replaces: Nothing. No step checks where light landed today.
rungs.tested: Scripted scene changes on the Hue bulbs and the displayed incumbent scenes, with the light model's prediction for each applied scene, read on the next metering frame after the last step that actually went out has settled, under rung 7's probe rule, with occupied seconds flagged. Frames taken mid-fade or mid-move are excluded. Occupied metering first appears at rung 7, not here. Aim verification for the spot (E9) waits for a gimbal fixture, its capability qualification {{dec:fixture-capabilities}} and the owner's approval for physical output [[R11]].
rungs.gate: Tolerance **±15%**, hit rate **≥ 85%**, writing the verify block on the Decision and the residual on LightState; residuals are taken against the prediction for the actual resulting state (case V11: after A's dim, the applied scene predicts 368 lx at counter-1 until a re-solve, and LightState ls-190409's 357 lx is a −2.9 % residual with no drift flag), and a held or superseded channel is excluded from misses and never flagged as drift. The share of misses explained (daylight, a person shadowing the board, drift) is reported; the verify shadow explanation uses the nominal body envelope. No eye point is ever written as verified: per-point status and unverifiable coverage are reported, and the spill and increment checks at visible other-person regions each carry their measurement uncertainty, with bounds fixed before the run. A fallback patch is a verify aid only, never delivered service. The verifiable share of gold need time at the owner's marks is reported, because it bounds delivered-service evidence at rung 11. Each metric's orientation and δ are fixed before the run {{dec:promotion-margins}}.
rungs.loop: Not yet: verify residuals first matter at rung 11, where they can roll a canary back.
rungs.unblocks: A real-light canary that can roll itself back.

rungs.name: Hand the bulbs to the coordinator
rungs.replaces: den_lighting as the bulbs' sole automatic writer, driven by occupancy, a Steam gaming scene and per-fixture holds that end 2 minutes after the later of vacancy and the latest touch or, in a game, when the game ends; during a game, vacancy turns held bulbs off without ending their holds, and game exit clears every hold and restores the pre-game normal snapshot [[R14]]; it records any change it did not command as a manual hold, and outside gaming as its new normal scene, even while paused.
rungs.tested: A live canary on the four Hue bulbs (`actuation = shown`), with the owner's go-ahead. Its hold behaviour, whether other bulbs may make up for a held one and so what the re-solve after a hold may do, is not admitted until the owner decides {{dec:compensation}}; the canary's option is to be chosen from rung 9's replay report (recommended, pending). Coordinator writes go through den_lighting or carry a context it recognises as its own (A11's command log); pausing den_lighting is not enough. The incumbent is frozen as read statically from its source: den_lighting manifest 1.0.4, `VACANCY_SECONDS` 120, the gaming scene at 38/255 at each bulb's warmest white, its hold semantics and `resume_automatic` [[R14]]; its installed version and its automatic and gaming switches are read from its status sensor before rung 0 logging. Before each block: write the incumbent's normal snapshot, call `den_lighting.resume_automatic` (it clears holds and drives each fixture to den_lighting's current normal, or its gaming scene), then check that the status sensor shows no holds, no gaming and qualified occupancy. Candidate-block writes and corrections never become den_lighting's normal scene; whether a manual level keeps becoming a bulb's normal under the coordinator is open {{dec:normal-scene}}. Game time is open {{dec:gaming}}: with non-gaming strata and handback (recommended, pending), the bulbs go back to den_lighting in both arms while a game runs, and that time and a washout after it are outside the comparison. Also tested: a hold arriving between solve and send (the held bulb's step is dropped under every option; whether another bulb's step still goes out depends on whether a local checker may complete it {{dec:local-completion}} and, where one may, on the compensation option, as does the re-solve that follows); hold-lifetime parity with den_lighting (a change to the lifetime is open {{dec:hold-lifetime}}); Hue execution parity, an OFF or a new level during a fade with no old retry and a late own report repaired once (V9i–V9j); gaming entry and exit under a hold (V63: under P0 and the mode forms of P1–P3 the free bulbs make den_lighting's moves; under P1-strict, unlike den_lighting, after a dim hold the free bulbs stay off from game-time vacancy until the game ends, and under a brighten hold no free bulb reaching the footprint turns off for game-time vacancy; P2-strict makes those moves only in part, and P3-strict acts as P1-strict where the free bulbs reach the changer's task points; at game exit every option matches only with the pre-game snapshot restore; in the first canary, under non-gaming strata with handback, den_lighting owns game time in both arms {{dec:gaming}}); a held bulb predicted over the glare limit (V65(a)) {{dec:manual-vs-safety}}. The expected results of the hold-between-solve-and-send case and V63 follow the compensation option, and V63's live run also the gaming option, so they are not admitted as pass or fail until the owner decides {{dec:compensation}} and, for V63's live run, {{dec:gaming}}. Corrections record `changes[]` and `whose_light`.
rungs.gate: Fewer corrections per occupied hour than the frozen den_lighting policy within the compared stratum: the lower bound of the oriented CPH improvement's interval is above 0 (superiority under A13's convention {{dec:promotion-margins}}), with human actions that opened or replaced a hold, one per Correction, as the numerator [[R14]] and occupied hours under one occupancy rule in both arms as the denominator [[R1]]. On a pre-registered, arm-blind gold sample of canary sessions, missed service per occupied hour, unserved-need minutes per hour (`hold_limited` is present only under P1–P3, and there every `hold_limited` minute counts inside it except a known changer's in their own episode {{dec:compensation}}) and delivered service coverage are non-inferior to the incumbent's under A13 Gate 1's rule, all measured at the owner's marks, and missing-geometry rates do not differ between arms (if they differ, the service comparison is insufficient, not passed) {{dec:service-floors}} {{dec:delivered-statistic}} {{dec:reference-geometry}}. Design: A13's illustrative rates need about 150 occupied hours per arm if corrections are independent, and about 300 at an exposure-adjusted φ = 2 (illustrative); φ is the Pearson dispersion of a quasi-Poisson fit to whole-session counts, corrections counted one per human action, with a log(occupied hours) offset; rung 0's incumbent log gives a planning value, and the canary re-estimates it in both arms; the allocation unit, strata and reset rules are fixed before the run. Rollback under every option: free channels of an applied scene predicted over a hard glare limit, or raising their part of an open `hard_conflict`; glare reports or AR10 attributions per hour above the bound fixed before the run (A13) {{dec:comfort-policy}}; verify residuals against applied-scene predictions jumping; or rescues per hour, the gold-free proxy, above their bound. A held light alone predicted over the limit is logged and reported as conflict minutes; only under S1, or S2 outside an exception, does a held-light conflict still open past the owner-set deadline also roll back {{dec:manual-vs-safety}}. No rollback cites a measured glare value. Per A13, the per-link checks carry most promotion decisions; this end-to-end rate confirms them.
rungs.loop: Non-inferior on every touched link per A13 Gate 1; each metric's orientation and δ fixed before the run {{dec:promotion-margins}}, and none is set yet.
rungs.unblocks: Per-person light on the real bulbs outside game time (under non-gaming strata with handback, recommended, pending {{dec:gaming}}), and real corrections against real decisions for attribution. A complete-policy comparison, with gaming reproduced as an externally signalled mode and the pre-game snapshot restored at game exit, is still needed before any permanent handover.

rungs.name: Correction attribution
rungs.replaces: Manual holds that only pause a light; nothing learns from them [[R14]] [[R16]].
rungs.tested: E1: a few weeks of logged corrections from the canary, then a hand-sorted sample of them, whose hand labels include 'cannot tell' and whose light it was; fixtures for a shared bulb, a scene button, an isolated spot and an unknown changer.
rungs.gate: Per update path, the precision of the cases that would update, counting a match only when the link, `whose_light` and the key all agree with the hand sort, admitted at a pre-registered lower bound; the forced-update rate under a gated upper bound; coverage and abstention by stratum (channel class, known or unknown changer, one versus two or more present) {{dec:attribution-thresholds}}. A six-class **Cohen's κ** (the five links plus 'cannot tell'), with a session-bootstrap interval, is reported per rule class with counts and abstentions; the old five-link κ ≥ 0.6 is reported beside it, never as the admission test on its own. AR10 (comfort) cases are scored only against changer reports, otherwise reported as unreferenced, and no AR10 case ever updates `Preference.offsets` {{dec:comfort-policy}}.
rungs.loop: Not yet: attributions are read by the later preference rung.
rungs.unblocks: Preferences from corrections whose light can be isolated (comfort-attributed corrections excepted), and whether corrections may train need and perception {{dec:learning-permissions}}. On four room bulbs almost every two-person correction abstains (AR11), so per-person learning may have little admissible data until a fixture can light one person alone.

later.name: Preferences
later.gate: Regret per correction falls to the person's own noise, learning inside the seed look's guardrails. Colour offsets are learned, stored and applied in mired (`mired_shift`, positive = warmer); how today's kelvin guardrail translates is open {{dec:colour-guardrails}}. Comfort limits only tighten {{dec:comfort-policy}}.

later.name: Execution timing
later.gate: Fades within ±0.5 s of plan. On engineered fixtures, only after their stop, aim-readback and fade-pre-emption capabilities are measured {{dec:fixture-capabilities}}.

later.name: Structured-slot student
later.gate: Replaces Qwen for routine moments only through A13's promotion gates on the gold set, demand scored per band as well as by calibration, at about 100 ms of processing and GPU memory far below Qwen's ~48 GB (A6, A8). The edge budget itself is not set.

later.name: Session appearance
later.gate: Only if geometry-only tracks miss E2's gate, and only after the owner's decision on rebuild principle 15 (A5) {{dec:learning-permissions}}.

later.name: Looks from a designer
later.gate: Simple weights on perceptual terms are enough (E11); designers agree with each other more than users do (E12); looks transfer between rooms (E14).

later.name: Self-calibration
later.gate: Each experiment's own question: zone orientation measured, the tape worksheet retired, safe entity mapping, the scan made optional.

later.name: Spatial memory
later.gate: Use labels the room (E19); memory only ranks hypotheses, never evidence.
